newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia 1997 corn output seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 1997 corn output seen rising.

text.p: Indonesia's corn production is expected to increase to about 10.5 million tonnes in 1997 from 9.1 million tonnes last year, Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah told Reuters on Monday.
"Production will be close to 10.5 million tonnes this year," he said. "It is much higher than last year's production of 9.1 million tonnes."
He also said he wanted the government to impose an import tariff on corn because of poor domestic prices.

"I will talk with related ministers to implement the import tariff on corn. The domestic price seems to have dropped due to pressure from corn imports," he said. "I don't know what the government decision will be. Just wait."
He declined to say how much import duty he was seeking.
An agriculture ministry official said last week Baharsyah had written to Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad asking for the import tariff on corn to be reviewed, but had yet to receive a reply.
Traders said the move, if implemented, would have a significant impact on importers as they would have to pay higher prices for their imported corn, thus raising production costs.
Indonesia, in a bid to reduce its dependence on imported corn, has embarked on an ambitious programme to boost local production through the cultivation of a high-yielding hybrid.
A agriculture ministry official said in January that a total of 885,000 hectares would be planted with the hybrid variety this year, and another 900,000 hectares in 1998.
Traders said said Indonesia imported around 1.6 million tonnes of corn in 1996.
They said 1997 imports were expected to remain at last year's level because the success of the hybrid project had been overstated and that corn demand was growing rapidly.
